title: OpenAI reverses course and backs open models - TCR 07/27/26
description:
Nvidia launched the Open Secure AI Alliance with Palantir, IBM, CrowdStrike, and Hugging Face as OpenAI reversed its stance to back open models, China's CXMT debuted on Shanghai's STAR Market up 470% to a roughly $487 billion valuation, and Anthropic and Andon Labs released Drone-Bench testing whether AI can autonomously fly a $129 drone to find and follow a person.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-july-27-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:44 Open Secure AI Alliance and OpenAI's reversal
8:12 CXMT challenges the memory oligopoly
11:56 Anthropic's Drone-Bench autonomous flight
16:59 Texas water plan and the gas-plant notice
24:34 Close

This episode covers the Open Secure AI Alliance and OpenAI's reversal, CXMT's challenge to the Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron 90% memory lock, Anthropic's Drone-Bench autonomous-flight benchmark, Texas deferring data-center water accounting to 2032 alongside a Clean Air Act notice against Vantage and VoltaGrid gas plants, and an explainable framework predicting acute kidney injury 24 hours out across 140,637 admissions.

The day's signal is a contest over who gets to hold capability, and whether concentrating it in a few hands is still the winning bet. Nvidia turned an open letter into a named institution as Palantir, IBM, CrowdStrike, and Hugging Face signed on to call open models defensive assets, and OpenAI crossed the line it was named after by joining the camp warning against blanket restrictions. That same pull toward diffusion reached the memory substrate, where CXMT's 470% debut aimed a funded fourth supplier at a three-firm oligopoly. Anthropic and Andon published Drone-Bench so autonomous flight can be measured on a $129 rig before it deploys, with no model yet completing the full route. Underneath the contests, verified capability moved toward people: an explainable two-model framework predicted acute kidney injury 24 hours out with a positive predictive value near 0.7, and IIHS found Waymo in 68% fewer crashes across 50 million miles. Texas, meanwhile, approved a five-year water plan that declines to forecast data-center draw until 2032, while a Clean Air Act notice forced off-grid gas emissions back onto the ledger.
